qualities.name: Eloquent
qualities.definition: the line makes one point, exactly. A spiritual or abstract idea is explained in plain words, or anchored to something concrete in the same sentence or the next. A long line earns its length by explaining, never by stacking adjectives.
qualities.check: does it say one thing exactly, with every abstract idea anchored?

qualities.name: Refined
qualities.definition: confident and unhurried. No hype words, no stacked exclamation marks, no pun that strains. A wink or a cultural reference is welcome when it is precise and lands without being explained. Spiritual practice is spoken of as ordinary life, never as spectacle.
qualities.check: would it sit at ease beside a prestige brand, with any wink landing on its own?

qualities.name: Sensual
qualities.definition: the line gives the reader something to see, touch, smell or feel (light, texture, a place, a ritual), and it is warm toward the reader. A piece's story uses only what the product database carries; where it is from and how it is made are claims until HLR's signer rules (ledger HLR-O01, HLR-S01).
qualities.check: can the reader picture or feel something, and is it warm without flirting?

qualities.name: Real
qualities.definition: the line names a specific, recognizable moment or feeling from everyday life, in words a friend would use. Lofty language is balanced by plain language in the same piece. It never promises perfection or a transformed life.
qualities.check: is there a moment the reader knows from their own week, said plainly?

qualities.name: Uplifting
qualities.definition: the reader leaves a little more hopeful or grateful. The piece inspires first, and the product follows as the natural next step, never as the opening demand. Encouragement is specific and sincere, never cheer that could be said of anything.
qualities.check: does it lift the reader before it sells, with nothing that could be said of anything?

review_tiers.what: your own record lines; read-only evidence (inventories, censuses, measurements, screenshots); [documented] and [observed] values with their sources; null roles with gaps and owners; new tests, lints, census terms and scans; fixes inside an unreleased engine version
review_tiers.ships_on: the checks for what changed, plus one fresh-context review with no open blocker or should-fix; record lines and read-only evidence need only the author's re-read of the diff

review_tiers.what: the open gates (2 and 4) and the forge proof's grade; any [derived] value used as law (tokens, the contrast law, voice principles, the taxonomy, house style); every Figma write and every convention, and any write to the client's live files; engine design choices, which ship as marked defaults he rules on; an engine release to install; scope, channels and deliverables; a fan-out or squad run its prompt does not already authorize (estimate first); overwriting a canonical file or one outside your write scope; anything that leaves this brand home for HLR; a finding still open after three rounds
review_tiers.ships_on: tier 1, then his explicit go as a dated DECISIONS line

review_tiers.what: HLR's facts and rights: the HLR-owned questions in the DECISIONS line "Gate 1 closed" (2026-10-17), from positioning and claims and the font licenses to the origin and karat claims; HLR's confirmation of Eddie's Gate 1 picks; claims marked needs_legal, which a person signs
review_tiers.ships_on: tier 2, then HLR's answer recorded with its source and date; until then the role stays null with its gap
review_tiers.go: HLR, at a live review or in writing, relayed by Eddie

never_ships: Never ships, at any tier, and no waiver covers it: an invented figure, claim, price, quote or review; another brand's name, fact, file key or taste; a write to the client originals or the reference copy; an unconfirmed face without its flag, or an image without its usage right and without its placeholder; an em dash in our own text in copy or a deliverable (verbatim client text, as section 2 lists it, keeps its punctuation).
production_rule: In production, once HLR's team runs the forge, checks flag and never block shipping: a person decides (playbook section 4). In this build, an open blocker or should-fix stops its release until it is fixed or Eddie rules.

brief.title: Brief: the made-to-order pendants (demo email for Review 2)

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Introduce four of HLR's made-to-order pendants to the email list and send each reader to a pendant's page.

sections.heading: Audience
sections.text: HLR's email subscribers. No segment data is on file (HLR, Review 1).

sections.heading: Message
sections.text: Each of these pendants is made to order: it is made after you choose it.

sections.heading: Products
sections.text:
- The Element Pendant (lead)
- The Sacred Pendant
- The Genesis Pendant
- The Seeker Pendant

Names, kinds and the made-to-order fact come from brand-pack/products.json (catalog snapshot 2026-10-17, observed). The product descriptions are empty, so the copy states no material, karat, stone meaning, size or price.

sections.heading: Channel and deliverable
sections.text:
Email, content type product_listing (the registry's sections: header, hero, text block, product grid, footer). One 1200 master on 04 Staging, built from HLR Library modules in the type’s observed order (template 2:683: header, hero, two-column text, product grid, footer), plus the cleared editorial band and a closing CTA; sent as image slices.

Send date: 2026-11-05, a demo date for Review 2 only.

sections.heading: Must say
sections.text: Nothing beyond the footer disclaimer, which the footer carries verbatim (HLR-REQ-01).

sections.heading: Guidance
sections.text:
- Vocabulary: made to order; pendant. No line on how, where or by whom a piece is made beyond made to order: products.json carries only that, and the rest is ledger HLR-O01 until HLR’s signer rules.
- Tone: the voice contract as written; short lines; one accent word in a headline.
- Notes: no figures. Intentions only as tradition or intention ("worn as a reminder to"), never as a promised effect (ledger HLR-M rows).

sections.heading: Never say
sections.text: Nothing beyond the pack's prohibited patterns.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Visual: hero image, the photos page node 27:137 (HLR Editorial, a hand with two chains and a pendant, dark ground); grid, the packshots 27:174 (The Element Pendant), 27:210 (The Sacred Pendant), 27:206 (The Genesis Pendant), 27:191 (The Seeker Pendant); an editorial image for a full-bleed band, 27:136. All cleared by Eddie (DECISIONS 2026-10-23).

routes.angle: The making is the story: each pendant is made after you choose it, one at a time.
routes.tension: Jewelry usually waits on a shelf; these wait for the person who will wear them.
routes.weakness: No product description is on file, so the making cannot be shown in detail: the route carries one fact and leans on the images.

routes.angle: A pendant worn as a reminder of what you are calling in.
routes.tension: An intention set in the morning is gone by noon; something worn stays.
routes.weakness: Metaphysical framing waits on HLR's C2 ruling; every line stays intention, never effect, and the ledger lists it for paraphrase review.

routes.angle: The giving season: a piece made for one person, chosen for one person.
routes.tension: Gifts in November are bought in a rush; a made-to-order piece is chosen on purpose.
routes.weakness: No order cutoff or delivery window is on file, and made-to-order timing makes any by-the-holiday promise a claim nobody can back.
